name: Ochre Editorial Deck
description: A style-locked HTML deck for publishing reviews and executive reporting. It pairs assertive editorial headlines with precise charts, cool-paper layouts, and restrained ochre accents.
whatYouGet: Consistent editorial layouts across the full deck
Action-led headlines and clearly labeled evidence
Readable charts, figures, captions, and source notes
goodFit: Executive reviews built from verified source material
notFor: Inventing data to fill reporting gaps
requiredInputs: Required sections or preferred slide count

faq.q: Can I provide rough notes instead of a slide outline?
faq.a: Yes. Provide the notes and identify the audience and decision. The deck will organize the material into an evidence-led narrative without changing verified facts.

faq.q: What happens when a figure has no source?
faq.a: It is flagged for confirmation or omitted. The deck does not present invented figures as reported results.

demoPrompt: /sl-ochre-editorial-deck Create exactly 9 slides for North District Publishing, a fictional regional studio. Frame Q2 around paid-readership growth, retention risk, editorial findings, and a three-step retention test, ending with three editorial choices and next-cycle actions. Use Ochre Margin style. Quote the title “PAID READERSHIP GREW, BUT RETENTION NEEDS ATTENTION.” and closing title “APPROVE THE RETENTION TEST BEFORE THE NEXT CYCLE.”
followUpPrompts: Make the chart takeaway more explicit without changing the figures.
Shorten the copy for a five-minute executive readout.
Add source notes to each slide that uses the subscriber table.
externalCostNote: No external services. Runs entirely on your agent.
